**Deal notes added by Anders Holm 2026-09-03:**

Closed lost. The picklist is going to say No decision and that is the least useful thing I could write, so here is what actually happened.

There was never a deal. The champion resigned a week before our discovery call and I did not know. He answered every question fully precisely because he had already left in his head and had nothing to manage. My best discovery of the year was a man with nothing to lose talking to somebody who was finally interested.

He has not been replaced. His work has been split between the production manager and the sales director and the environment part has gone to neither, because it was never on an organisation chart, it was his because he picked it up nineteen years in. Nothing will happen until the next template arrives and then somebody will fill it in with a trade association average, which is where this started in March.

Two things he did before he left, both because I asked him to, and both worth more to them than anything they would have bought from us.

He called the mill. They hold regional origin on about eighty percent of intake, by delivery, collected since 2024 because a Danish customer asked. The supposedly impossible part of this project was already solved and nobody at Hedlunds had made one telephone call in two years. His words: once you have not done a thing for a year it stops being a task and becomes a fact about the world.

He asked for the range review pack. There is a sustainability section, there is a footprint column, there are three competitors in it and Hedlunds appears in it with the indicative March numbers, unsupported, and lower than two competitors. He flagged it to their sales director who asked whether they were wrong, and the honest answer is that they are not wrong, they are unsupported, and he could not explain the difference in a corridor on his second to last day.

**Range review is 6 October.** If anybody asks a question about that column, the sales director rings us in the second week of October wanting it done by Christmas. If nobody asks, nothing happens and it repeats next year with a longer form. That is his prediction and he knows them better than I do. Diarised.

The sentence I cannot get away from, and I am putting it in here rather than in Slack because I want it in the account: we arrive at exactly the moment the problem has become too big for the one person carrying it, holding the solution, and by then that person has already lost the internal argument. Two years ago this was three questions long and an hour a week would have fixed it. Nobody was talking to them two years ago because there was nothing to sell.
